cogs_cases.note: The primary model uses 41.2% for the current 6/6/6 core food mix. The 33% figure is never substituted into primary results.

gst.revenue_treatment: All restaurant dine-in sales and the modelled hot takeaway, coffee and alcohol sales are treated as taxable. Gross sales include GST; P&L revenue is gross divided by 1.10.
gst.cost_treatment: P&L costs and upstream fit-out values are shown excluding GST where recoverable. Input credits require valid tax invoices and correct tax codes. Basic food inputs may be GST-free. Wages have no GST.
gst.rent_treatment: The rent GST basis is UNKNOWN for all three qualified properties. Calculator rent is entered ex GST and no rent input credit is claimed in the GST cash proxy.
gst.net_gst_payable_treatment: Output GST is calculated, but net GST payable is UNKNOWN because taxable input proportions and rent GST are not established.

superannuation.basis: Modelled as 12% of cash wages. Actual qualifying earnings, exclusions and employee eligibility require payroll review.
superannuation.payment_timing: Payday super applies from 1 July 2026 according to the current official source.

payroll_tax.post_official_period_treatment: The $1.2m threshold and 5.45% rate are carried forward as an INFERRED calculator assumption after 30 June 2027 and must be refreshed.
payroll_tax.taxable_payroll_basis: Cash wages plus employer super. Group wages, contractors, interstate wages and other liable amounts are UNKNOWN.
payroll_tax.threshold_assumption: Non-grouped employer, all wages in NSW and entitled to the full threshold. This is not established because the operator entity and group are unknown.
payroll_tax.monthly_method: Monthly accrual applies 5.45% to taxable payroll above a daily-prorated annual threshold. Annual reconciliation may differ.

income_tax.reason: Company and personal income tax are excluded because entity structure, ownership, financing and taxable income are unknown.

scenarios.name: Cosmetic reuse of verified hospitality shell
scenarios.entry_condition: Existing food use, grease arrestor, compliant exhaust, HVAC, fire measures, accessible path, sanitary facilities, hot water and adequate utilities are all proven suitable for Buono. Existing movable equipment is assigned no value unless separately tested and transferred.
scenarios.evidence_state: INDICATIVE_MODEL; ONLY VALID AFTER ALL ENTRY CONDITIONS PASS

scenarios.name: Moderate hospitality adaptation
scenarios.entry_condition: Hospitality use and basic wet services are plausible, but exhaust, grease, HVAC, finishes, fire, services and customer flow need material upgrade or replacement.
scenarios.evidence_state: INDICATIVE_MODEL; REQUIRES SITE AND DESIGN VALIDATION

scenarios.name: Heavy conversion or failed-services shell
scenarios.entry_condition: Existing claims fail, use changes materially, or the premises needs new exhaust route, grease system, HVAC, utility infrastructure, access/fire work, comprehensive surfaces and a cool room.
scenarios.evidence_state: INDICATIVE_MODEL; HIGH UNCERTAINTY BEFORE INTRUSIVE DILIGENCE

35c-ross-forest-lodge.rationale: The upstream operations model starts at moderate adaptation and requires escalation if services fail.

186-lyons-drummoyne.rationale: Cosmetic reuse is only valid if every entry condition passes. Those conditions remain unverified, so moderate adaptation controls the alpha cash model.

294-lyons-russell-lea.rationale: The upstream operations model uses a moderate placeholder pending interior inspection and requires escalation if services fail.

Site-level demand, conversion, capacity and observed daypart transactions are not measured.
Owner compensation and opportunity cost are excluded from shop EBITDA.
Entity structure, group status and post-2026/27 payroll tax settings are unknown.
Input GST credits cannot be calculated without tax-coded supplier and property invoices.
Fit-out scenarios exclude unpriced critical items and depend on physical and documentary diligence.
